# Scene encoders

<!-- slot-head:begin (generated by tools/make_method_pages.py; do not edit) -->
<div class="gp-chips"><span class="gp-chip">Seed-based · 5 methods</span><code class="gp-chip">--set backbone=</code><span class="gp-chip">47 options</span></div>
<!-- slot-head:end -->

The scene encoder is the first learned stage of a seed-based method: it turns the point cloud
of one depth view into one feature vector per point. Its reach and resolution decide what a seed
knows about its surroundings before any crop is taken.

## Use it

<!-- method-options:begin (generated by tools/make_method_pages.py; do not edit) -->

=== "GraspNet-baseline"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e \
        --set backbone=ptv3 -o graspnet-baseline_ptv3.yaml
    grasppanda compose graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e --list backbone
    ```

=== "GSNet"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set backbone=ptv3 -o gsnet_ptv3.yaml
    grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list backbone
    ```

=== "Scale-Balanced-Grasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e \
        --set backbone=ptv3 -o scale-balanced-grasp_ptv3.yaml
    grasppanda compose scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e --list backbone
    ```

=== "EconomicGrasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set backbone=ptv3 -o economicgrasp_ptv3.yaml
    grasppanda compose economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list backbone
    ```

=== "FineGrasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose finegrasp/finegrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set backbone=ptv3 -o finegrasp_ptv3.yaml
    grasppanda compose finegrasp/finegrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list backbone
    ```

The first command writes a checked config; the second lists every option of the slot under that method, with what was measured. Then `grasppanda probe <file>` tries the config on real frames and `grasppanda train <file>` trains it ([Swap a component](../get_started/swap.md)). Each method page lists the same: [GraspNet-baseline](../methods/graspnet_baseline.md#backbone) · [GSNet](../methods/gsnet.md#backbone) · [Scale-Balanced-Grasp](../methods/scale_balanced_grasp.md#backbone) · [EconomicGrasp](../methods/economicgrasp.md#backbone) · [FineGrasp](../methods/finegrasp.md#backbone).

<!-- method-options:end -->

??? note "What the columns say, and who is left out"

    - **Runs**: out of the methods the option is a swap under, those under which its probe trained on real frames without error. A method that ships the option is named *own* and not counted; a method still undecided is counted and named. Measured on 20 training iterations on 8 RealSense frames of GraspNet-1Billion (one scene), seed 0, one run per cell; nothing was measured on GraspClutter6D or on Kinect frames.
    - [How we measure](../evidence/index.md) defines every word of these columns.

    Who is left out, and why:

    - `feature-propagation`, runs: an adapter: compose inserts it where the next stage needs it, so it is measured inside the cells it was inserted in; inserted in 65 cells (43 runs, 18 runs-empty, 4 refused).
    - `furthest-point-subsample`, runs: an adapter: compose inserts it where the next stage needs it, so it is measured inside the cells it was inserted in; inserted in 90 cells (54 runs, 36 runs-empty).
    - `image-painted`, runs: point painting: a wrapper written into a config by hand (compose does not write it); no probe record.
    - `image-painted-subsampled`, runs: point painting: a wrapper written into a config by hand (compose does not write it); no probe record.

??? note "Sources and licences"

    *Code base*: the upstream repository, commit and licence that `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` lists for the class's file (code adapted from it, or a module tree that follows it so that its weights load); *written here*: no third-party code. *Extra*: the optional install the class needs ([every extra](../get_started/installation.md)). *Output*: where the features live and how many channels the preset returns; compose sets a free `out_channels` to the width the method's other stages need. Released weights carry licences of their own.

## Choosing

- **Change as little as possible:** an encoder of the kind the method has needs no adapter.
  Otherwise compose inserts `FeaturePropagation` or `FurthestPointSubsample` and says so.
- **The width:** compose sets `out_channels` to the width of the encoder it replaces where the
  encoder has that option, so the other stages keep theirs.
- **Room-scale settings:** most of these networks were published for rooms or streets. The
  presets restate radii and grids for a table top by analogy; they are starting points, not
  tuned values.
- **Released weights** are an initialisation trained on other data, often under their own
  licence; each family page lists the files that load and what does not.
- **Optional libraries:** a config that names a missing library passes the config check and
  stops when the model is built, with the install line.

## Details

??? note "Input and output"

    ```python
    class Backbone(nn.Module):                # grasppanda/models/base.py
        output: "dense" | "subsampled"        # where the returned features live
        in_channels: int
        out_channels: int
        def forward(self, points: PointSet, feats: Tensor) -> PointFeatures: ...
    ```

    | | |
    |---|---|
    | `points` | `coords (N, 3)` in metres in the camera frame, all clouds of the batch concatenated with batch offsets; a table-top view has 15 000 to 20 000 points about 5 mm apart. |
    | `feats` | `(N, in_channels)`: constant ones, coordinates and normals, or nothing, as the method feeds; compose sets `in_channels` to match. |
    | output `dense` | one feature per input point, bound to the same point set. |
    | output `subsampled` | features on a sub-sample, the same number for every cloud of the batch; those points become the seeds. |
    | `out_channels` | the width of the features, injected into the proposal, the view stage and the grouper. |

    Three contracts tie an encoder to its neighbours; `grasppanda compose` resolves each or
    refuses with the fix:

    1. **Where the features live.** A proposal requires `dense` or `subsampled` features; for
       the other kind compose wraps the encoder in an adapter and says so.
    2. **The point features.** Compose sets the encoder's `in_channels` to what the method
       feeds.
    3. **The width.** An encoder declares the width it returns, a grouper the width it needs,
       and the config check compares them without building anything. Under
       Scale-Balanced-Grasp a fixed width gets the projected grouper
       ([Grouper](grouper.md), "The width of the seed features").

    No contract checks the unit of length: the header of every preset says what its radii and
    grids were derived from.

??? note "Probing under Scale-Balanced-Grasp"

    A probe of Scale-Balanced-Grasp needs the reference's width histogram, which cannot be
    built from the eight frames of a probe; without it the probe ends as `wired` (a synthetic
    scene). Import the file once (`configs/scale_balanced_grasp/README.md`), then:

    ```bash
    grasppanda probe <config> --opts data.train.dataset.scale_statistic.source=legacy_import \
        data.train.dataset.scale_statistic.reference_sha256=<SHA-256 of the reference's file>
    ```

Scene encoders checked against the code their authors published (PTv3 and its variants,
LitePT, PointNet2) are on
[Encoders checked against their authors' code](../model_zoo_backbones.md).
